issues.source_quote: Козадоев Геннадий Петрович
issues.translation_quote: Gennady Petrovich Kozodoyev
issues.justification: The film's running joke is Lyolik's mangling of the surname (Козлодоев/Казладоев, 'goat-molester'). The translation renders the name flatly and keeps 'Kozlodoyev' with no explanation, so the insult and the gag are lost on an English audience.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, в нашем деле гланое - этот самый реализм!
issues.translation_quote: As our dear boss says, in our line of work, realism's the thing!
issues.justification: The boss's catchphrases ("как говорит наш дорогой шеф") are comic parodies of proverbs. Several are rendered literally or flattened, e.g. 'if a man's an idiot, it's a lifelong condition', and 'strike while the iron's hot, right at the cash register', which loses the pun on the original idiom. The humor is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Что они ни делают - не идут дела! Видно, в понедельник их мама родила.
issues.translation_quote: Looks like they were born on a Monday night.
issues.justification: The 'Monday is a hard day' superstition is the song's core joke and the rhyme is partly preserved, but 'Monday night' alters the sense (mother gave birth on Monday) and the chorus later relies on cancelling Mondays. The image is blurred, and the lyric 'нет календаря' becomes 'no calendar in sight', which is weaker.

issues.source_quote: Ну-ка иди отсюда, Миша! Как у вас там говорят, топай до хазы.
issues.translation_quote: Now get out of here, Misha! How do you people say it? "Get back to your pad."
issues.justification: Underworld slang ('хаза', criminal lair) is turned into the mild, 1960s-hip 'pad', and the mockery of the criminal's jargon is lost.

issues.source_quote: Нет, на это я пойтить не могу!
issues.translation_quote: No! I ain't goin' along with that!
issues.justification: The speaker's mock-hick dialect works as a comic disguise as the 'taxi driver'. Here it is overdone with 'ain't', and elsewhere ('Jus' like we agreed', 'I didn't do nothin'') the dialect marking is inconsistent and drifts into a US/English-regional register that does not match the Soviet setting.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках! Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: Drop dead! I hope I see you in your coffin, wearing white slippers! May you live... on nothing but... your salary!
issues.justification: The curse is an Odessa-style comic rant with deliberately non-standard grammar ('у гробу, у белых тапках'). The translation is standard English and loses the dialectal comedic voice, and the final curse is clumsily broken up.

issues.source_quote: Фрис-стрит, рыбна улица, - Аптека «Чиканук»
issues.translation_quote: Fris Street, Fish Street, - Chikanuk Pharmacy
issues.justification: Deliberately garbled foreign names (the characters rehearsing pseudo-foreign addresses) are neutrally transliterated, with no sense of the mangled pseudo-language.

issues.source_quote: Цигель, цигель, ай-люлю
issues.translation_quote: Zigel, zigel, ai-lyu-lyu
issues.justification: The transliteration changes between 'zigel', 'tsigel' variants and is inconsistent with the Russian-based transcription used elsewhere in the pseudo-foreign passages.

issues.source_quote: Нет, шуба подождёт. Я считаю, главное - это поглядеть мир! А то действительно работает, работает...
issues.translation_quote: Otherwise it's work, work, work...
issues.justification: 'Действительно' is dropped and the speaker's meaning is blurred; the remark about 'one just works and works' is rendered impersonally.

issues.source_quote: Ну разве можно!...
issues.translation_quote: You can't do that!
issues.justification: This line follows the Mickey-style hubbub about the boy; its context and the Russian 'unacceptable' sense are weakened. Similarly, 'Ну что же это такое' becomes 'What was that for?'.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: Such is "c'est la vie," as they say abroad.
issues.justification: The original deliberately gender-mangles 'сё ля ви' as a comedic foreign phrase; the English loses that error.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a stack of tickets and you just might win a... Waterworks!
issues.justification: The rhyme (пачку/водокачку) is lost, so the comic sloganeering effect disappears.

issues.source_quote: Пьянству - бой!
issues.translation_quote: Down with drunkenness!
issues.justification: The Soviet slogan parody is rendered adequately but 'бой' (fight) martial flavor is lost.

issues.source_quote: Ну что Вы, Семён Семёнович... Спокойно… Выпейте!
issues.translation_quote: Come now, Semyon Semyonovich... Calm down... Have a drink!
issues.justification: Slightly stiff for a spoken captain's persuasion, though acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Сенья, Ой, как Вы меня напугали!
issues.translation_quote: Oh, you frightened me!
issues.justification: Minor; the seductive Hotel scene's suggestive 'послушайте, как бьётся сердце' is OK, but 'Следить за сигналом' etc. is unaffected.

issues.source_quote: Печёнкой чую, клюнула настоящая рыба.
issues.translation_quote: I can feel it in my gut: we've hooked a real fish.
issues.justification: 'Печёнкой' (liver) is idiomatic and is generalised to 'gut', which is acceptable but loses flavor.

issues.source_quote: Лэйтинант. Старшой я…
issues.translation_quote: Lootenant. Senior...
issues.justification: The mock-dialect is only partially carried over and 'Старшой я' loses its colloquial sense.

issues.source_quote: Оригинальное конструктивное решение позволяет вам легко превратить пиджак... в куртку!
issues.translation_quote: Its ingenious design lets you easily turn the blazer... into a jacket!
issues.justification: The joke is that the 'transformation' is absurdly trivial; the English still works, but the prior 'Универсал-69' award and bureaucratic fashion-show parody is somewhat flattened.

issues.source_quote: Сеня, про зайцев... Это не актуально!
issues.translation_quote: Senya, rabbits? That's old hat!
issues.justification: 'Rabbits' for 'зайцы' is accurate, but 'old hat' is a British idiom jarring with the American register elsewhere.

issues.source_quote: Здравствуйте... - Здравствуйте. - Э... скажите, пожалуйста, Ваше имя-отчество...
issues.translation_quote: your name and patronymic, please?
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the English 'patronymic' is stilted for subtitles.

issues.source_quote: Х-х-х-х-ха... Но и Вы, тоже едете за границу в первый раз?
issues.translation_quote: And is this your first trip abroad too?
issues.justification: The humor of the radio interview misinterpretation ('Нет, я никуда не еду') is slightly weakened by the added 'too'.
